=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- scripts/mcp_handshake_probe.py:206-218 | severity=high | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [x-ai_grok-4_1-fast]
  PROBLEM: stderr is captured via PIPE but never drained during the handshake wait loop.
  WHY: A chatty server or wrapper can fill the stderr pipe buffer, block the child, and make a healthy server appear to time out.
- scripts/mcp_handshake_probe.py:155-160 | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [x-ai_grok-4_1-fast]
  PROBLEM: The response-size cap is checked after extending the buffer, so a single read can push the buffer past the documented limit.
  WHY: This can transiently exceed the cap and weakens the intended bounded-memory guarantee.
=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===

- scripts/mcp_handshake_probe.py | severity=high | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: stderr is captured via PIPE but never drained/read during the handshake wait loop.
  WHY: Servers emitting >64KB of startup diagnostics to stderr can fill the pipe buffer, block the child, and prevent stdout response, causing false probe timeouts.
- scripts/mcp_handshake_probe.py | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: Buffer cap check runs post-extend, allowing transient overshoot by a full read chunk.
  WHY: This can briefly exceed the documented 1MiB cap and weakens the bounded-memory guarantee.
